recentItems.title: Episode 3 of 3: Crime as a Service (AUDIO ONLY)
recentItems.description:
Who knew a murder-for-hire would be so complicated? This remarkable, undercover conversation with an admitted member of the Ulster Volunteer Force, a paramilitary organization from Northern Ireland, lays out the grizzly logistics of a contract killing. No detail is too small: the cost, the location, the weapons. There’s a cold calculus to it: each choice affects the odds of a clean kill and the attendant risks of being found out. This is true crime playing out in real time.

recentItems.title: Episode 2 of 3: Partners in Crime (AUDIO ONLY)
recentItems.description:

recentItems.title: Episode 1 of 3: Flag of Convenience (AUDIO ONLY)
recentItems.description:
It all starts with an undercover meeting about a murder for hire. An admitted member of a Northern Irish paramilitary group called the Ulster Volunteer Force, the UVF, says he can arrange to have a man killed. So, we travel to Belfast to track him down. In this episode, Al Jazeera Investigates the violent factional history of the UVF and how the organization has evolved and expanded since the 1998 Good Friday peace agreement. What happens to paramilitary group when the fighting stops? They don’t go away, they adapt and in the case of the UVF, it has become a violent, international drug cartel willing to sell its services to the highest bidder.

This episode was written and produced by Kevin Hirten with Simon Boazman and Craig Pennington who is also the audio editor. Additional editing by Manny Panaretos. recentItems.title: The UK's Far Right & Loyalist Hitmen: Fake Rallies & Murder | Al Jazeera Investigates
recentItems.description:
This Al Jazeera Investigation exposes the dangerous links between the right-wing student movement Turning Point UK (TPUK), which has organised and participated in anti-immigrant protests in the UK, and a member of a paramilitary group who can arrange murders for money.

An undercover team of journalists investigated the secret network of right-wing activists and far-right groups accused of fueling the violent anti-migrant protests on Britain’s streets.

Turning Point UK is an independent offshoot of the powerful right-wing US political activism group Turning Point USA. TPUK’s leader is revealed to have links to the UK Conservative Party and Reform Party, and is secretly filmed arranging a fake political rally with members of the British far right and brokering an extraordinary murder for hire plot.

The team exposes the links between culture war activists and members of the Northern Irish loyalist group the UVF, which is proscribed by Britain as a terrorist organisation.

recentItems.title: The UN isn't broken. It was designed this way | Al Jazeera Explains
recentItems.description:
From Gaza and Ukraine to Sudan, the United Nations has repeatedly faced criticism for failing to stop wars and protect civilians. But what if some of its most controversial failures are not flaws in the system, but consequences of how it was designed?

In 1945, the world’s most powerful countries struck a bargain: they would join a new international organisation, but retain the power to block major Security Council decisions.

More than 80 years later, that arrangement still shapes global diplomacy.

Al Jazeera explains how the UN veto works, why five countries hold extraordinary power over international peace and security, and why reforming the Security Council remains so difficult.

The question isn’t simply why the UN fails to act. It’s whether the world can change a system built to accommodate its most powerful countries.

recentItems.title: Israel faces legal reckoning at the ICC and ICJ over Gaza genocide
recentItems.description:
Israelis head to the polls on October the 27th - at a time when it's more isolated than ever before.
On top of sanctions and broken diplomatic ties, the country is facing a potential legal reckoning on the international stage.
Its genocidal war on Gaza has been livestreamed on social media and broadcast on television around the world.
The Israeli military has not been held accountable, but the wheels of international justice are starting to turn.

Al Jazeera’s Step Vaessen reports from The Hague, Netherlands.
